title: Overreliance on AI in Information-seeking from Video Content
abstract: arXiv:2603.19843v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The ubiquity of multimedia content is reshaping online information spaces, particularly in social media environments. At the same time, search is being rapidly transformed by generative AI, with large language models (LLMs) routinely deployed as intermediaries between users and multimedia content to retrieve and summarize information. Despite their growing influence, the impact of LLM inaccuracies and potential vulnerabilities on multimedia information-seeking tasks remains largely unexplored. We investigate how generative AI affects accuracy, efficiency, and confidence in information retrieval from videos. We conduct an experiment with around 900 participants on 8,000+ video-based information-seeking tasks, comparing behavior across three conditions: (1) access to videos only, (2) access to videos with LLM-based AI assistance, and (3) access to videos with a deceiving AI assistant designed to provide false answers. translated_title: 从视频内容中获取信息时对人工智能的过度依赖
translated_abstract: 多媒体内容的普及正在重塑在线信息空间，尤其是在社交媒体环境中。与此同时，搜索正在被生成式人工智能迅速变革，大语言模型（LLM）被常规性地部署为用户与多媒体内容之间的中介，用于检索和总结信息。尽管其影响力日益增长，LLM的不准确性和潜在脆弱性对多媒体信息检索任务的影响在很大程度上仍未被探索。我们研究了生成式人工智能如何影响从视频中检索信息的准确性、效率和信心。我们在8000多个基于视频的信息检索任务上对约900名参与者开展了实验，比较了三种条件下的行为：（1）仅可访问视频；（2）可访问视频并获得基于LLM的AI辅助；（3）可访问视频并获得一个旨在提供错误答案的欺骗性AI助手。我们发现……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 通过约900名参与者、8000多个视频信息检索任务的实验，本研究揭示了用户在借助基于LLM的AI辅助（甚至面对故意提供错误答案的AI助手）从视频中检索信息时存在对AI的过度依赖现象。
en_tdlr: Through an experiment with around 900 participants on 8,000+ video-based information-seeking tasks, this study reveals users' overreliance on LLM-based AI assistance—even when the AI deliberately provides false answers—when retrieving information from video content.
